literal: In the midst of battle, those who die are easy to find; rare are those who do not fear in the midst of an assembly.
translation: Those who can face death in the midst of battle are easy to find; but those who can stand without fear in the midst of an assembly are truly rare.
modern: போர்க்களத்தில் சாகக்கூடியவர்கள் எளிதாகக் கிடைப்பார்கள்; ஆனால் அவையின் நடுவே அச்சமின்றிப் பேசக்கூடியவர்கள் கிடைப்பது அரிது.
explanation: This couplet contrasts physical bravery in battle with intellectual courage in a public assembly. The author notes that many soldiers are willing to face death on the battlefield, making such brave individuals relatively common. However, standing before a learned assembly without fear requires a different, rarer kind of courage. The key words 'பகை' (battle) and 'அவை' (assembly) represent two different arenas of human trial, highlighting that mental fortitude before peers is scarcer than physical valor.
